m2c/tests/secret_handling/secret_fakes.py -- Patch C15: fake secrets and ordinary developer text, built at run time.

WHY EVERYTHING HERE IS ASSEMBLED WHEN A TEST RUNS
-------------------------------------------------
This repository's pre-commit hook and CI run gitleaks, and m2c/tests/ is not on its allowlist.  So no string in this
directory may look like a real credential as a literal: every fake below is joined from short pieces, or drawn from a
seeded random generator, when it is CALLED.  ``_cat`` is a function on purpose: ``"gh" + "p_" + ...`` in a function
body is folded by the Python compiler into one contiguous constant (and lands in the .pyc file, where gitleaks looks
too), a call to ``_cat`` is not.

The fakes are random, not hand-picked, so the tests exercise the detectors on values nobody chose.  Every random body
is given at least one digit and one letter (``_mixed``): a real 32-character key lacks a digit with a chance below one
in a thousand, and the detectors that need a digit say so in their documentation.

``Fake.secret`` is the part that must never survive redaction; ``Fake.text`` is a realistic line around it.

m2c/tests/secret_handling/test_secrets_corpus.py -- Patch C15: the false-positive budget, stated and enforced.

THE BUDGET
----------
Redaction has two ways to be wrong.  A false negative leaks a credential to the server; it is the failure this whole
patch exists to prevent, so the budget for it is ZERO on every kind the detectors claim: the secret corpus below
(built at run time from random pieces, 30 kinds x 40 seeds) must be caught 100 %.  A false positive hides a harmless
span from the model, which then has to ask the person for it: annoying, never dangerous.  So the budget for it is a
ceiling, not zero, and it is set from how often a developer's tool output is actually hit:

* ``FALSE_POSITIVE_LINE_BUDGET = 0.5 %``: at most one line in two hundred of the ordinary-text corpus may be changed.
  The corpus is deliberately hard (about a third of its lines contain a word like ``password`` or ``token``), so
  real output, which is mostly logs and source with far fewer such words, is hit much less often than that.
* Git commit hashes (any length), SHA-256 digests and UUIDs are NEVER redacted, anywhere in the ordinary text
  (zero tolerance, asserted per category): the model needs them to read ``git log``, lock files and traces.

The categories of ordinary text: git hashes and logs, checksums, UUIDs (also next to credential words), base64 images
(also next to credential words), lock files, minified code, long identifiers, source code full of credential-shaped
words, logs and tra

Positive: each kind of secret (built at run time, see secret_fakes.py) is replaced by a marker that names only the
kind, the text around it is untouched, and the findings carry a kind and a count and nothing else.
Negative: near-misses and ordinary code are left alone.  Also: Unicode evasions, idempotence, the fail-closed path.

m2c/tests/secret_handling/test_secrets_runner.py -- Patch C15: redaction at the outbound boundary of the runner.

THE SCRIPTED SESSION
--------------------
Canary secrets (fake, built at run time) are planted in project files and in the environment; a scripted session
runs through C24's real ``ToolRunner`` (real tools, real shell, real policy) against the fake link, which checks every
payload against the protocol schemas.  The assertion that matters: no canary (nor any 8-character window of one)
appears in ANY ``tool_result`` output, ``tool_stream`` chunk or edited-call line the link was handed.

THE OTHER HALF: THE TERMINAL
----------------------------
What the person sees locally is not redacted.  The runner's executor is wrapped by a tap that records what the tools
really produced, and what ``on_chunk`` was given, BEFORE the boundary: those still hold the canaries.  (In this version
the person's terminal shows tool activity from the runner's own callbacks and the server's run events, never from the
outgoing copy; the redaction happens only on the copy that leaves.)

m2c/tests/secret_handling/test_secrets_stream.py -- Patch C15: the stateful stream redactor.

A secret split across two (or twenty) chunks must not leak: every kind, at every split position, fed in two pieces
and one character at a time, with and without a closing newline.  The stream result must equal the one-shot result.
